summary: Barrière will open Fouquet's Gstaad on 4 December 2026, the sixth Fouquet's address, in a property built as an Ultima flagship. It offers 11 suites and 6 apartments (33 bedrooms), a 1,500 m² private chalet, a spa of more than 800 m² and a Zuma pop-up. Ultima Capital keeps the real estate and Barrière operates.
title: Fouquet's Gstaad to open on 4 December

visual_text.rest: brings its Fouquet's brand to Gstaad, opening on 4 December.

why: A French luxury brand enters the Swiss Alps through an owner–operator partnership rather than a purchase.
body_long:
Fouquet's Gstaad opens on 4 December 2026. It will be the sixth Fouquet's address, after Paris, New York, Courchevel, Saint-Barth and Mykonos, which opened only a few months earlier.

The hotel is in Saanen, within the Gstaad resort area, one of the most discreet mountain destinations in Europe. It was originally built as a flagship for the Ultima group. Under a strategic partnership between the two groups, Ultima keeps the property and Barrière Collection operates it under Fouquet's, its ultra-luxury brand.

## Built for long Alpine stays

The hotel has 11 suites and 6 apartments, for a total of 33 bedrooms, as well as a nine-bedroom private chalet of 1,500 square metres. Rooms have mountain views, fireplaces, contemporary art and light-filled balconies.

The spa covers more than 800 square metres, with a 15-metre indoor pool, sauna, hammam, indoor and outdoor jacuzzis and a snow shower. Five treatment rooms, including a double suite, use Augustinus Bader products. The fitness area includes Technogym equipment, two Pilates reformers and a yoga studio.

Dining opens with a Zuma pop-up serving contemporary Japanese cuisine: sushi, sashimi, wagyu and robata dishes, with an open kitchen, a bar and a heated outdoor terrace.

## A brand born on the Champs-Élysées

Fouquet's traces its origins to 1899 on the Champs-Élysées. Barrière Collection, founded in 1912 by François André and developed by Lucien Barrière, Diane Barrière and Dominique Desseigne, is now chaired by Alexandre Barrière and Joy Desseigne-Barrière.

## The signal

In the Alps, an owner no longer needs to sell to change its brand. A partnership lets it keep the asset while a recognised operator brings distribution, loyalty and a name guests already know from Paris. For French brands, it is a fast route into Swiss winter demand, and Gstaad completes a mountain pair with Courchevel.

Congratulations to the Barrière and Ultima teams on this new chapter.
